To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein synthesis machinery is organized into two functionally independent subunits, that these subunits are located on different ribosomes, that the subunit containing the catalytic machinery is the 50S subunit, that the subunits can be dissociated and reassociated, and that the dissociation and reassociation can be carried out in the presence of the protein synthesis machinery.

(1) protein synthesis is an energy-dependent, membrane-mediated process; (2) protein synthesis is a process that is regulated in a complex way, and that this regulation is not confined to the ribosomes; and (3) the ribosomal subunits are the functional units of protein synthesis, and not the ribosomes themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of protein biosynthesis.
understanding how the cell controls the fidelity of protein synthesis, which is a fundamental process for the maintenance of the integrity of the genome and for the regulation of gene expression.
the development of a model of protein synthesis in Staphylococcus aureus.
